text:
Samir: perf CI flagged a regression on PR #5291 — token_throughput_seq128 microbench +12% (over threshold). CI run: https://ci.redwood/runs/5291/bench
Jia: saw that. quick glance shows kernel_selector changes landed recently, but also scheduler PR 5248 adjusted batch_wait_ms. either could explain it. :thinking:
Pranav: ran `benchctl compare` locally: p95 went from 21.3ms -> 24.0ms for seq128, throughput -11%. bisecting now.
perf-ci-bot: benchmark-regression: test=token_throughput_seq128 delta=+12.1% threshold=+10% (job=eng-runtime/bench-5291)
Elena: if scheduler reduced wait, maybe we have smaller batches hitting kernels not optimized for batch_size=1-3. also possible more KV cache copy overhead per request. can someone dump batching histograms?
Samir: bisect points to commit d4e7b2f — "scheduler: reduce batch_wait_ms 6->3ms" (merged in release/1.8). that lines up with timeline.
Pranav: did a quick `perf record` on CI-like instance. top samples show more memcpy / kernel launches:
```
# perf top (sample)
23.4%  libcudart.so memcpy
18.1%  runtime.cu::launch_kernel
12.7%  serving::dispatch_batch
 9.3%  kv_cache::copy_prefix
```
Looks like overhead per kernel increases with more small batches.
Jia: metric dump from the failing run shows `batch_size.histogram` shifted: median 8 -> 3, p90 12 -> 5. more single-item batches.
Elena: could also be kernel_selector fallback — if batch_size < 4 we pick the non-batched kernel which is slower for seq128. check `kernel_policy.py` conditions and quantized kernel availability.
Samir: good point. I tested locally toggling selector to prefer batch-optimized kernel for seq>=2 and the microbench improves ~6%. but not full regression. reverting batch_wait_ms makes it go back to baseline in CI.
Pranav: created temp revert branch `revert/scheduler-5248` and kicked off bench job: https://ci.redwood/bench/7890. also opened a draft patch that adjusts selector to prefer batch kernels when estimated batch_size >= 4 (WIP).
Jia: long-term we should make wait adaptive to arrival rate not a fixed ms. and add a guard in kernel selector to prefer batch kernels when dispatch sees bursty arrivals. filing PERF-341 for follow-up.
perf-ci-bot: bench job 7890 completed: regression resolved on revert branch, delta now -1.0% vs baseline.
Samir: great — merging revert to unblock release. follow-ups: (1) make adaptive wait heuristic (PERF-341), (2) tighten kernel_selector tests in microbench CI, (3) add instrumentation for per-request kernel choice. I'll file PRs. :tada:
